answer: Each AI agent boots inside a TEE that signs a hardware‑bound key, and the key is registered on the lantern ledger as a unique forge‑stamp tied to that enclave’s measured code hash. When a falcon node requests service, it presents the signed stamp; other nodes verify the attestation chain and reject any duplicate stamps, so an attacker must provision a separate physical TEE for every identity, costing roughly $200 per enclave and a mandatory 24‑hour hardware lock‑up per identity.
